checks.evidence_note: Seed id matches psi-map.json entry for PSI-23.
PSI-23 proposalTitle is 'Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames'; ACME overview uses 's-Flame' shorthand.
Common shorthand forms (s-Flame, s-Flames, ACME s-Flame) are reasonable variants of the official name.
psi-map.json maps acme-s-flames to PSI-23; challenge brief lists six ACME experiments.
PSI-23 flightProgram is ISS with investigation dates 2015-2019; flown on ISS.
PSI-23.json exists locally with full record; psi-map.json confirms mapping.
Standard PSI detail page URL pattern for PSI-23.
PSI-23 flightProgram field is 'International Space Station (ISS)'; ACME overview confirms ISS.

PSI-23 objective lists three specific objectives (A, B, C) covering transient structure, extinction limits, and pulsating instabilities for soot-free and sooty flames; ACME overview paraphrases as advancing prediction of structure/dynamics/extinction. Extracted text is an accurate synthesis.

PSI-23 is basic combustion science (flame structure, kinetics, extinction limits); challenge brief says ACME's secondary objective is fire prevention but s-Flame itself is fundamental research. 'fundamental' is a valid schema value.
PSI-23 SubResearch Area is 'Flames of gaseous fuels'; approach uses gaseous fuel/inert mixtures; challenge brief states ACME experiments featured flames of gaseous fuels.

PSI-23 approach names hydrogen, methane, ethylene as fuels; nitrogen, helium, carbon dioxide as diluents. Experimental table (PSI-23.csv) shows fuel bottles: 100% H2, H2/CH4 blends, 50%/45% CH4 and C2H4 in N2, H2/CH4/C2H4 diluted with He.

PSI-23 approach: 'mixtures of gaseous fuels and diluents issued into an oxidizing environment through a spherical porous burner and ignited to obtain a nominally spherical, one-dimensional stabilized flame.' ACME overview confirms porous spherical burner.
PSI-23 experimentHardware is 'Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME'; challenge brief confirms ACME used CIR.
PSI-23 approach describes spherical porous burner; ACME overview describes constant-volume ~90 L chamber insert with modular ACME hardware.
psi-map.json lists five other ACME experiment ids (acme-bre, acme-cld-flame, acme-e-field, acme-cfi-g, acme-flame-design); challenge brief says six ACME experiments shared hardware.

PSI-23.csv Atmosphere* column shows '~21% O2 with N2/He' and '~30% O2 with N2/He' across 18 test rows. Extracted min 21, max 30 is a correct parse of the approximate values. Confidence 'medium' appropriate for text-parsed approximations.

PSI-23.csv notes 'Atmosphere is ~1 atm' (no numeric pressure column). 1 atm = 14.7 psi. ACME is constant-volume so pressure rises with vitiation. Extracted single point 14.7 psi with 'low' confidence and note is appropriate.
PSI-23.csv has no airflow column; PSI approach mentions reactant (fuel) flow rates only. Correctly left null with unknown confidence.
PSI-23 projectType is 'Microgravity Investigation'; flight platform ISS. Challenge brief: spherical flame only possible in microgravity. Value 0 g with high confidence is correct.
PSI-23 approach names nitrogen, helium, carbon dioxide as diluents. Experimental table shows N2 and He in fuel and chamber atmosphere.

PSI-23 objective tests H2/CH4/diluent and C2H4/diluent ratios at different flow rates. Experimental table shows two rounds varying fuel bottle composition and chamber atmosphere (~21% vs ~30% O2, N2 vs He).
Inferred from investigation design: single platform (ISS), single burner geometry, shared ACME hardware in CIR. Medium confidence appropriate for inference.

PSI-23 approach lists spectrally resolved images, flame/burner temperatures, radiative flux, system operating conditions (flow rates, temperatures, pressures, acceleration). ACME overview details specific instruments (imaging arrays, radiometers, PMTs for OH*/CH*, gas chromatograph, pressure, SAMS-II). Medium confidence appropriate as instrument set is for shared ACME hardware.
Marked 'inferred' confidence; synthesizes PSI/ACME fundamental objectives against brief's fire-safety framing. Note acknowledges this is own synthesis.

PSI-23 researchImpacts: diffusion flame understanding improves power, efficiency, pollutant emissions, reliability. ACME overview: primary goal is improved terrestrial combustion efficiency and reduced emissions.
